definition: A neural network trained to compress input data into a lower-dimensional representation and then reconstruct the original input from it.
details: Autoencoders are used for dimensionality reduction, denoising, and as building blocks for more advanced generative architectures like VAEs.

explainer.lead: An autoencoder learns to squeeze data into a compact code and then rebuild the data from that code. This makes it useful for reducing dimensions, removing noise, and learning representations that can support more advanced generative models.

tiers.eli5: Imagine shrinking a detailed drawing into a short set of instructions, then using only those instructions to draw it again. An autoencoder practices both jobs until the new drawing looks much like the original. The short instructions keep important patterns while leaving less room for every detail.
tiers.practitioner: Train the encoder and decoder together by comparing each reconstruction with its target, using a bottleneck smaller than the input. For denoising, provide corrupted inputs and train toward clean targets. A small code can discard information needed for accurate reconstruction, so check reconstruction quality rather than assuming compression preserves everything.
tiers.paperLevel: An encoder f_theta maps input x to a lower-dimensional code z = f_theta(x), and a decoder g_phi produces x_hat = g_phi(z). Training minimizes a reconstruction loss L(x, x_hat), with corrupted inputs and clean targets used for denoising. The bottleneck forces selective compression, so information absent from z cannot be recovered reliably by the decoder.

explainer.example: A grayscale image containing 784 pixel values can be encoded into 32 numbers, then decoded back into 784 values. Training adjusts both networks so the reconstructed image resembles the original, while the 32-number code provides a much smaller representation.

usedIn.name: Dimensionality reduction
usedIn.detail: The learned code represents high-dimensional input with fewer numbers.

usedIn.name: Denoising
usedIn.detail: The network learns to reconstruct clean data from corrupted input.

usedIn.name: Generative architectures
usedIn.detail: Autoencoder ideas provide building blocks for variational autoencoders.

components.name: Encoder
components.detail: Transforms the input into a lower-dimensional representation.

components.name: Code
components.detail: The compact intermediate representation, also called the bottleneck.

components.name: Decoder
components.detail: Reconstructs an output in the original input's form from the code.

flow: The encoder compresses it into a lower-dimensional code.
The decoder reads only that code.
The decoder produces a reconstruction of the input.
Reconstruction error guides training of the encoder and decoder.
explainer.lineage: Autoencoders serve as building blocks for more advanced generative architectures, including variational autoencoders.
explainer.whyItMatters: The architecture learns compact representations without requiring a separate hand-designed compression rule. The same encode-and-reconstruct structure supports both dimensionality reduction and denoising.

diagram.caption: Data passes through an encoder, a compact code, and a decoder before reconstruction error guides training.
